Collectively, these amendments are intended to strengthen the Town’s land-use regulations to protect Exeter’s groundwater resources, natural resources, environmental quality, and rural character. text: TOWN OF EXETER, RI PLANNING BOARD 675 Ten Rod Road Exeter, RI 02822 Ph: (401) 294-2592 EXETER PLANNING BOARD NOTICE OF SITE VISIT and PUBLIC HEARING(S) SITE VISIT WHEN: TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 22, 2026 - 5:00 p.m. WHERE: Site Visit at 576A Nooseneck Hill Road, Exeter, RI (applicant: RAM 576, LLC) Following the conclusion of the site visit, the Planning Board will reconvene at 6:00 p.m. the same day (September 22, 2026) at the Town Hall Council Chambers, 675 Ten Rod Road, Exeter, RI NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARINGS WHEN: TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 22, 2026 - 6:00 P.M. WHERE: EXETER TOWN HALL – COUNCIL CHAMBERS 675 TEN ROD ROAD, EXETER, RI 02822 AGENDA I. II. III. CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL: OLD BUSINESS: NONE NEW BUSINESS: A. SITE VISIT – MAJOR LAND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (On-site 5:00 p.m.) Applicant and Owner: Property Location: Assessor’s Zoning District: RAM 576, LLC 576A Nooseneck Hill Road, Exeter, Rhode Island Plat: 46, Block 2, Lot 3 Light Industrial (LI) The Exeter Planning Board will conduct a Site Visit on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. at the project site located at 576A Nooseneck Hill Road, Exeter, Rhode Island. RAM 576, LLC, of 1160 Post Road, Suite 4, Warwick, RI 02888, is the Applicant and Owner of the approximately 15.4-acre property zoned Light Industrial (LI). The Applicant proposes a Major Land Development Project consisting of a warehouse and office building, along with associated outdoor areas for construction material stockpiling, processing, and equipment storage. The application seeks approval of a combined Master Plan and Preliminary Plan. The purpose of the site visit is to satisfy the requirements of Section 6.5 – “Site Visits” of the Exeter Land Development and Subdivision Regulations. 1|Page The site visit will give Planning Board members an opportunity to observe existing site conditions and special features, identify potential site design considerations, and informally discuss site design concepts. Members of the public are permitted to attend. However, the Planning Board will take no formal action during the site visit. Any comments or observations made by Planning Board members during the site visit shall be considered informal and shall not be construed as a decision, determination, or final action on the pending application. B. NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING- MAJOR LAND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT – COMBINED MASTER PLAN AND PRELIMINARY PLAN – 6:00 P.M.- EXETER TOWN HALL – COUNCIL CHAMBERS Applicant and Owner: Property Location: Assessor’s Zoning District: RAM 576, LLC 576A Nooseneck Hill Road, Exeter, Rhode Island Plat: 46, Block 2, Lot 3 Light Industrial (LI) The Applicant and Owner, RAM 576, LLC of the property identified as Assessor’s Plat 46, Block 2, Lot 3, located at 576A Nooseneck Hill Road, Exeter, Rhode Island, is proposing a Major Land Development Project consisting of a warehouse and office building, together with associated outdoor areas for construction material stockpiling, processing, and equipment storage. The application seeks approval of a Combined Master Plan and Preliminary Plan for the proposed development, encompassing approximately 15.4 acres zoned Light Industrial (LI). The application is being reviewed pursuant to the Town of Exeter Land Development and Subdivision Regulations (LDSR), Section 6.8 – “Major Land Development Projects and Major Subdivisions.” C. NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING – MAJOR SUBDIVISION WITH DIMENSIONAL VARIANCE, WAIVERS AND COMBINED MASTER PLAN AND PRELIMINARY PLAN REVIEWED AS A UNIFIED APPLICATION Owner/Applicant: MDF REALTY LLC Property Location: 0 Stony Lane, Exeter, Rhode Island Assessor’s: Plat: 12 Block: 4 Lot: 4 Zoning District: RU-4 Total Parcel Area: Approximately 129.44 acres Proposed Development: Creation of one (1) new approximately four-acre lot through a frontage cut. The Exeter Planning Board will conduct a Unified Development Review pursuant to the Exeter Zoning Ordinance and Land Development Regulations (LDR). The Planning Board will consider a request for a Dimensional Variance, followed immediately by a combined Master Plan and Preliminary Plan Public Hearing for a proposed Major Subdivision, including requested dimensional relief and waivers. The proposed subdivision, known as The Flood Plat, involves the creation of one (1) new approximately four-acre lot for residential development through a frontage cut from Assessor’s Plat 12, Block 4, Lot 4, containing approximately 129.44 acres in the RU-4 Zoning District. The property has frontage on Stony Lane, a Town roadway, and is located at 0 Stony Lane, Exeter, Rhode Island. 1. DIMENSIONAL VARIANCE – FRONT YARD SETBACK The purpose of the first Public Hearing is to discuss and/or act upon the Applicant’s request for the following dimensional variance: a. Front Yard Setback: A dimensional variance from Section 2.4.2(4) of the Exeter Zoning Ordinance, which requires a minimum front yard setback of one hundred (100) feet. 2|Page The Applicant is requesting twenty-five (25) feet of dimensional relief, resulting in a proposed front yard setback of seventy-five (75) feet. The requested relief is attributed to the wetland buffer located to the rear of the proposed lot. 2. MAJOR SUBDIVISION – COMBINED MASTER PLAN AND PRELIMINARY PLAN Following the Dimensional Variance Public Hearing, the Planning Board shall discuss and/or act upon the combined Master Plan and Preliminary Plan application for a Major Subdivision, pursuant to the Exeter Land Development Regulations. The Applicant is requesting consideration of the following waivers: b. Waiver – Master Plan Site Visit: A waiver from LDR Sections 6.5 and 6.8.1(c), which require a site visit as part of the Master Plan review. The Applicant is requesting the waiver on the basis that the application proposes the creation of only one (1) new lot. c. Waiver – Traffic Study: A waiver from LDR Section 6.10.1.3, which requires the submission of a traffic study. The Applicant is requesting the waiver in connection with the proposed creation of only one (1) new lot. 3. PLANNING BOARD ACTION The Planning Board will consider the requested dimensional variance, waivers, and the combined Master Plan and Preliminary Plan application for the proposed Major Subdivision. Following the public hearing and review of the application, the Planning Board may approve, approve with conditions, or deny the applications in accordance with the Exeter Zoning Ordinance and Land Development Regulations. IV. ADMINISTRATIVE: A. Approval of Minutes – July 28, 2026 B. Future Meetings: 1. Planning Board Work Session Meeting – Tuesday, October 13, 2026 at 6 p.m. 2. Planning Board Regular Meeting –Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 6 p.m. V. ADJOURNMENT: The Planning Board shall allow oral and written comments from the general public at the Public Hearing. All public comments shall be made part of the public record of the project application. The proposal may be altered or revised prior to the close of the Public Hearing without further advertising, as a result of further study, or because of the views expressed at the Public Hearing. Any such alteration or revision must be presented for comment in the course of said Public Hearing. The application is available for review in person during regular business hours at the Exeter Town Hall Planning Office, 675 Ten Rod Road, Exeter, Rhode Island. By order of the Exeter Planning Board, Gina Thurn, Chairwoman. 3|Page

The motion to reconsider is one of the motions that can bring a question again before an assembly, and is designed to bring back for further consideration a motion which has already been voted on: If, in the same session that a motion has been voted on, but no later than the same day or the next day on which a business meeting is held, new information or a changed situation makes it appear that a different result might reflect the true will of the assembly, a member who voted with the prevailing side can, by moving to Reconsider [RONR (10th ed.), p. 304-321] the vote, propose that the question shall come before the assembly again as if it had not previously been considered. Legislative Findings and Intent. (a) The Town of Middletown is committed to increasing the safety and accessibility of its streets, roads and overall transportation systems for all users. (b) The benefits of adopting a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation to guide investments and decision-making for the Town’s transportation system to include increased safety and accessibility to multimodal transportation and access to destinations such as job centers and health or educational facilities; increased opportunity for active living, exercise, and recreation through waking and bicycling; economic benefits from walkable commercial areas and neighborhoods, better access to recreational areas, parks and beaches; and environmental, climate change and quality of life benefits. (c) The Town Council intends, by the enactment of this ordinance and the adoption of a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation, to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of all residents and visitors. 2. Definitions. – As used in this Ordinance. (a) “Green and Complete Streets” means an approach to transportation that calls for the planning, design, construction, maintenance and operation of streets, roads, highways, and other transportation facilities to serve multiple modes of transportation, to meet the needs of all users, including all ages and abilities, and to provide safe access and mobility while also incorporating green infrastructure elements. (b) “All Users” means all persons walking, rolling, bicycling, taking public transportation, driving or being transported by motorized vehicles or transportation freight or commercial vehicles, and includes persons of all ages and abilities. The Town Council of the Town of Scituate hereby ordains that Chapter 75 (“Zoning”), Article IV, Section 4.9 (“Floodplain District Regulations”), of the Code of Ordinances, Town of Scituate is hereby amended as follows: Note: Words set as strikeever are to be deleted from the ordinance; words set in underline are to be added to the ordinance. § 75-4.9. Floodplain District Regulations. (a) Basis for establishing Flood Hazard Areas. The Floodplain Overlay District is hereby established as an overlay district. The District includes all Special Flood Hazard Areas within the Town of Scituate designated as Zone A or AE on the Providence County Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) and Digital FIRM issued by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for the administration of the National Flood Insurance Program. The map panels of the Providence County FIRM that are wholly or partially within the Town of Scituate are panel numbers 44007C0260G, 44007C0270G, 44007C0277G, 44007C0280G, 44007C0290G., 44007C0295G, 44007C0385G, and 44007C0401G dated 03/02/2009, 44007C0289H, 44007C0402H, and 44007C0406H dated 10/02/2015 and 44007C0255H dated 06/23/2026. The exact boundaries of the District may be defined by the 100-year base flood elevations shown on the FIRM and further defined by the Providence County Flood Insurance Study (FIS) report dated 06/23/2026. The office of Emergency Management is responsible for floodplain management. The purpose of the Floodplain Overlay District is to ensure public safety: minimize hazards to persons and property from flooding: protect watercourses from encroachment; maintain the capability of floodplains to retain and carry off floodwaters: and facilitate the Town's compliance with the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968. as amended, and applicable National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) requirements. (b) Development regulations. The following requirements apply in the Floodplain Overlay District: Development within the Floodplain Overlay District shall comply with applicable FEMA National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) requirements, 44 CFR §60.3, and the Rhode Island State Building Code. A Floodplain Development Permit shall be required for all proposed development within the Floodplain Overlay District, including, but not limited to, construction, 93 94 95 96 97 98 99 100 101 102 103 104 105 106 107 108 109 110 111 112. 113 114 Lis 116 117 118 119 120 121 122 123 124 125 126 127 128 129 130 131 132 133 134 135 136 137 138 reconstruction, substantial improvements, placement of manufactured homes, placement of fill, and any other activities defined as development under applicable FEMA National Flood Insurance Program requirements. Prior to issuance of any building permit or Floodplain Development Permit, the applicant shall submit evidence of all permits and approvals required by federal or state law or by any other governmental agency having jurisdiction over the proposed development. The Town may establish a permit fee based upon the cost of construction, and an additional fee may be charged when professional engineering or other professional assistance is required for review of the application, to the extent authorized by applicable law. Floodplain development permit applications shall include sufficient information to allow the Floodplain Administrator to determine compliance with this ordinance, the Rhode Island State Building Code, and applicable NFIP requirements, including existing site contours, elevations of existing structures, proposed elevations, proposed grading and drainage, and other information reasonably required by the Floodplain Administrator. Development permits shall be reviewed for compliance with requirements concerning: materials resistant to flood damage: construction methods and practices that minimize flood damage: electrical, heating, ventilation, plumbing, air-conditioning, mechanical, sanitary and other service facilities designed or located to prevent floodwater from entering or accumulating within the components during flooding: and (iv) applicable elevation, floodproofing, anchoring, drainage and access requirements. Encroachments authorized within floodways shall comply with the Rhode Island State Building Code and applicable FEMA requirements. Where a regulatory floodway has not been designated. the Floodplain Administrator shall utilize the best available Federal. State. local, or other floodway data to determine whether proposed development would result in an increase in flood levels during the base flood. 139 140 141 142 143 144 145 146 147 148 149 150 151 152 153 154 155 156 137 158 159 160 161 162 163 164 165 166 167 168 169 170 171 172 173 174 175 176 177 178 179 180 181 182 183 184 Where FEMA has provided data from which a regulatory floodway may be designated, the Town shall administer and, where required. adopt the regulatory floodway consistent with applicable FEMA requirements and the principle that the regulatory floodway shall be designed to carry the base flood without increasing the water-surface elevation of the base flood by more than one foot at any point. No encroachment, including fill. new construction, substantial improvements, or other development, shall be permitted within a regulatory floodway where hydrologic and hydraulic analysis performed in accordance with accepted engineering practice demonstrates that the encroachment would result in an increase in flood levels during the base flood discharge. (2) Elevation and Construction Standards: All new construction and substantial improvements shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) where BFE data are provided by FEMA as determined from the effective FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM) and Flood Insurance Study (FIS). Where applicable under the Rhode Island State Building Code, the required elevation shall be the BFE plus the applicable State Building Code freeboard/design-flood-elevation requirement. Nonresidential structures and substantial improvements may, in lieu of elevation, be floodproofed below the Base Flood Elevation in accordance with FEMA requirements, provided that a registered professional engineer or architect certifies that the design and methods of construction are in accordance with accepted floodproofing standards. Where nonresidential floodproofing is proposed, the structure and attendant utility and sanitary facilities shall be designed, as applicable, to be watertight below the applicable flood elevation, with walls substantially impermeable to the passage of water and structural components capable of resisting hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loads and effects of buoyancy. The registered professional engineer or architect shall develop or review the structural design, specifications and plans and shall provide the certifications required by applicable FEMA and State Building Code requirements. Fully enclosed areas below the lowest floor shall be used solely for parking of vehicles, building access or limited storage. as permitted by the applicable building code and NFIP requirements, and shall be designed to allow the automatic entry and exit of floodwaters where required. Such enclosed areas shall not be constructed or used in a manner that would cause the structure to 185 186 187 188 189 190 191 192 193 194 195 196 197 198 199 200 201 202 203 204 205 206 207 208 209 210 211 212 213 214 215 216 PAM 218 219 220 221 222 223 224 225 226 227 228 229 violate applicable elevation or flood-resistant construction requirements. All new construction and substantial improvements shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse, or lateral movement of the structure. All electrical, plumbing, heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and mechanical systems shall be designed, constructed, or located to prevent flood damage in accordance with FEMA NFIP requirements and the Rhode Island State Building Code. Development within Special Flood Hazard Areas shall provide adequate drainage and safe access consistent with applicable FEMA, state, and local requirements. All public utilities and facilities associated with a subdivision or other development shall, to the maximum extent practicable, be located and constructed to minimize or eliminate flood damage. (3) Manufactured Housing Standards: Manufactured homes shall comply with FEMA National Flood Insurance Program requirements and the Rhode Island State Building Code. Placement of manufactured homes within designated floodways is prohibited except where the requirements of this ordinance, the Rhode Island State Building Code, and applicable FEMA National Flood Insurance Program regulations are satisfied. New or substantially improved manufactured home parks or subdivisions located within Special Flood Hazard Areas shall: (i) Provide stands elevated to or above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE); (ii) Provide adequate access and drainage; (iii) Ensure that piling or foundation systems are designed and constructed in accordance with applicable FEMA standards and the Rhode Island State Building Code, including placement in stable soil and provision of appropriate reinforcement where required for elevated structures. Elevated structures utilizing piles, piers, or similar foundations shall comply with FEMA construction standards and the Rhode Island State Building Code. Manufactured homes that are placed or substantially improved within applicable Special Flood Hazard Areas shall be elevated on a permanent foundation such that the lowest floor is elevated to or above the applicable flood elevation and shall be securely anchored to an adequately anchored foundation system to resist flotation. collapse and lateral movement, 230 231 232 233 234 235 236 237 238 239 240 241 242 243 244 245 246 247 248 249 250 251 202 253 254 255 256 257 258 259 260 261 262 263 264 265 266 267 268 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 consistent with applicable FEMA and Rhode Island State Building Code requirements. For manufactured homes located outside a manufactured home park or subdivision, in a new manufactured home park or subdivision, in an expansion of an existing manufactured home park or subdivision, or in an existing manufactured home park or subdivision where the manufactured home has incurred substantial damage as a result of flooding, the requirements of this subsection shall apply to the extent required by applicable FEMA and State Building Code requirements. (4) Subdivision Standards: Subdivision proposals and other proposed developments greater than fifty (50) lots or five (5) acres, whichever is less, shall include Base Flood Elevation data where such data has not otherwise been provided by FEMA. All subdivision proposals and other proposed developments within the Special Flood Hazard Area shall be designed to minimize flood damage, locate and construct public utilities and facilities to minimize or eliminate flood damage and provide adequate drainage to reduce exposure to flood hazards. (5) Zone A Standards (No BFE Areas): In areas designated as Zone A where Base Flood Elevation (BFE) data are not available, all new construction and substantial improvements shall be designed and constructed to be reasonably safe from flooding using best available flood hazard data, as determined by the Floodplain Administrator. In the absence of FEMA BFE or floodway data, the best available Federal, State, local or other BFE and floodway data shall be used as the basis for establishing applicable elevation and floodway requirements, including elevation of residential and nonresidential structures and floodproofing of nonresidential structures. (6) Flood Damage Reduction: All development shall be designed to minimize flood damage. (7) Utilities and On-Site Waste Disposal: Within flood-prone areas, new and replacement water supply systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the systems. New and replacement sanitary sewage systems shall be designed to minimize or eliminate infiltration of floodwaters into the systems and discharges from the 276 277 278 279 280 281 282 283 284 285 286 287 288 289 290 291 292 293 294 295 296 297 298 299 300 301 302 303 304 305, 306 307 308 309 310 311 312 313 314 315 316 317 318 319 320 321 systems into floodwaters. On-site waste disposal systems shall be located to avoid impairment to or contamination from such systems during flooding. (8) Change of Structural Use in Floodway: No person shall change the use of a structure or property located in the floodway of a Special Flood Hazard Area from business or commercial use to residential use where the change of use or associated expansion would increase the risk to occupants, except as otherwise authorized by applicable law and the Rhode Island State Building Code. (9) Detached Accessory Structures: Detached accessory structures in Zones A, AE, Al-30, AO and AH may be exempt from the elevation or dry-floodproofing requirements only where all of the following conditions are satisfied, to the extent such exemption is permitted by applicable FEMA and Rhode Island State Building Code requirements: The structure has a market value of less than $1,000: The structure has unfinished interiors and is not used for human habitation. (c) Floodplain Administrator Authority. The Floodplain Administrator is authorized to: (1) Review all development permits within the Floodplain Overlay District for compliance with this ordinance. (2) Determine applicability of FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps and Flood Insurance Studies. (3) Require submission of elevation certificates, floodproofing certificates, and other documentation required by FEMA, the Rhode Island State Building Code, or this ordinance where applicable. (4) Interpret Special Flood Hazard Area boundaries using the effective FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Map (FIRM), Digital Flood Insurance Rate Map (DFIRM), and related FEMA mapping products. (5) Maintain official floodplain regulatory records for the Town. (6) Review development proposals to determine whether such proposals are reasonably safe from flooding. (7) Maintain records of elevations, floodproofing certifications, engineering certifications, Letters of Map Amendment (LOMA), Letters of Map Revision (LOMR), Physical Map Revisions (PMR), and all other records required for National Flood Insurance Program compliance. (8) Notify adjacent communities, FEMA, the Rhode Island Emergency Management Agency (RIEMA), and other appropriate state and federal agencies prior to any alteration or relocation of a watercourse and maintain records of such notifications. (9) Verify that the flood-carrying capacity of altered or relocated watercourses is maintained and not diminished. (10) Require applicants to submit hydrologic and hydraulic analyses, engineering certifications, elevation certificates, floodproofing certificates, construction drawings, substantial-improvement or substantial-damage documentation, and other technical information reasonably necessary to determine compliance with this ordinance. (a) The animal warden may issue a violation notice to any owner or owners of any dog which violates any provision of this article or fails to cause a dog owned or kept by him to be licensed. The violation notice shall inform such person of the particular violation and that he shall pay the following charges: Unlicensed Dog (1st Offense) $25.00 Unlicensed Dog (2nd Offense) $100.00 Vicious Dog $10.00 $20.00 Vicious Dog harm to another domestic animal $10.00 $15.00 Vicious Dog bites human $20.00 $30.00 $25.00 $50.00 (each year) Dog Waste (non-removal) $50.00 Payment shall be made to the town treasurer by mail or in person, within seven (7) days of the date of the violation.
